# brink.watch

> An escalation barometer for pairs of states. For two dozen pairs it shows the
> escalation phase, a heat index of 0–100, the direction of change, and the gap
> between rhetoric and action. Everything is computed from open sources following
> a published methodology; every number opens down to the source event with a link
> to the publication it came from.

What separates this from other conflict trackers is one thing: it publishes the
record of its own errors. A backtest over nineteen conflicts that later escalated
caught 16 of 19, a median of 21 months ahead — while two alarms in three were
false, precision 32%. The number is uncomfortable, which is why it is published.

Three rules visible in the data itself:

- an unmeasured block is marked unmeasured, never replaced with a zero;
- raw events and the phase journal are append-only and cannot be rewritten;
- every pair shows its data coverage.

## Data (machine-readable, no key, no signup)

- [Full showcase](https://brink.watch/data/index.json) — every pair, the global
  index, and the day the numbers describe
- [A single pair](https://brink.watch/data/RUS-UKR.json) — heat broken down by
  block, phase history, raw source events with links. One file per pair in the
  register; the filename is the pair code
- [Backtest](https://brink.watch/data/calibration.json) — admission thresholds and
  the result of the check
- [Sitemap](https://brink.watch/sitemap.xml)

## Pages

- [Barometer](https://brink.watch/) — the world at large, and pairs grouped by phase
- [Pair page](https://brink.watch/dyad.html?id=RUS-UKR) — what the number is made
  of, phase history, source events
- [Methodology](https://brink.watch/#method) — what is computed and how
- [Terms of use](https://brink.watch/terms.html)
- [Privacy policy](https://brink.watch/privacy.html)

## What this is NOT

Not a war forecast and not a prediction of events. Not investment, legal or
military advice. Not the official position of any state or organisation. A heat of
50 means normal for that particular pair, not halfway to war.

## Citing

When quoting a number, give the date: values change daily, and a quote without a
date misleads. The underlying data belongs to its sources — UCDP, GDELT, OFAC, UN
General Assembly votes, ADS-B — and is distributed on their terms.

Contact: support@brink.watch
